name: Sessions Health vs Jane App
title: Sessions Health vs Jane App: EHR Comparison for Therapists (2026)
description: Compare Sessions Health and Jane App for mental health practices. See differences in pricing, features, telehealth, billing, and which EHR is best for solo therapists vs multi-disciplinary clinics.

summary.bottom_line: Sessions Health is purpose-built for mental health with transparent, affordable pricing (free to $39/month) and no hidden fees. Jane App is a Canadian-built multi-disciplinary platform with broader specialty support and more integrations, but at higher prices ($54-99/month). Choose Sessions Health for budget-conscious therapy practices; choose Jane App for multi-disciplinary clinics or Canadian practices.

key_differences.free_tier: Sessions Health (yes, 3 clients) vs Jane App (no)

sections.heading: Sessions Health vs Jane App: Overview
sections.content: Sessions Health and Jane App serve different niches in the EHR market. Sessions Health was founded by a practicing psychotherapist and is built specifically for mental health providers, emphasizing transparent pricing and ethical business practices. Jane App was built for multi-disciplinary healthcare clinics (physiotherapy, chiropractic, massage, mental health) and is particularly strong in Canada. While both handle scheduling, documentation, and billing, their target audiences and pricing structures differ significantly.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Sessions Health wins on pricing transparency and affordability. The platform offers a free tier for up to 3 active clients, then $39/month for unlimited clients. Additional practitioners cost $29/month each, and admin staff are unlimited and free. Jane App starts at $54/month for up to 20 appointments, $79/month for unlimited, or $99/month for advanced features. Jane's Insurance Billing add-on is $20/month. For a solo therapist, Sessions Health can be 50% cheaper than Jane App.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: Jane App has broader features for multi-disciplinary clinics: mobile apps, Zoom integration, Outlook calendar sync, and support for multiple healthcare specialties. Sessions Health is more focused on therapy workflows: it includes outcome measures (PHQ-9, GAD-7) and assessment tools designed specifically for mental health. Jane App requires a $15/month add-on for AI documentation; Sessions Health includes AI Assist. Neither platform supports e-prescribing.

sections.heading: Telehealth Comparison
sections.content: Jane App includes basic telehealth on all plans, with a $15/month upgrade for group telehealth features. Sessions Health charges $10/month for telehealth as an add-on, which includes HIPAA-compliant video, waiting rooms, screen sharing, and multi-participant support. If you need telehealth frequently, Jane's included basic telehealth is an advantage. However, Sessions Health's telehealth add-on at $10/month is still quite affordable.

recommendations.when: You're a solo therapist or small mental health practice prioritizing affordable, transparent pricing; you want therapy-specific features like PHQ-9/GAD-7 outcome measures; you have a very small caseload (free tier); or you're frustrated with price increases from other EHRs

You run a multi-disciplinary clinic with diverse provider types; you're based in Canada and need Canadian billing/PIPEDA compliance; you need a mobile app for on-the-go access; or you want broader calendar integrations (Outlook, Zoom)
You need e-prescribing (neither Sessions Health nor Jane App offers this) or you want a larger mental health-specific feature set with more EHR integrations

faqs.q: Is Sessions Health cheaper than Jane App?
faqs.a: Yes. Sessions Health offers a free tier (up to 3 clients) and costs $39/month for unlimited clients. Jane App starts at $54/month and goes up to $99/month. For solo therapists, Sessions Health can save $15-60/month compared to Jane App.

faqs.q: Does Sessions Health have a mobile app like Jane?
faqs.a: No. Sessions Health does not currently offer mobile apps for iOS or Android. Jane App has full mobile apps for both platforms. If mobile access is critical for your practice, Jane App is the better choice.

faqs.q: Which is better for mental health therapists: Sessions Health or Jane App?
faqs.a: Sessions Health is specifically designed for mental health therapists by a practicing psychotherapist. It includes therapy-specific features like PHQ-9 and GAD-7 assessments. Jane App supports mental health but was originally built for allied health (physiotherapy, chiropractic). For pure mental health practices, Sessions Health is often the better fit.

faqs.q: Can I switch from Jane App to Sessions Health?
faqs.a: Yes. Both platforms support data export. You would export client data from Jane App and contact Sessions Health support for import assistance. The 30-day free trial gives you time to evaluate Sessions Health before committing.
